comments.body:
Implemented as Gerrit change 2250 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2250
Commit b71e46660fa6 on branch `fe4e-shellcheck-gate`. **Verified +1** (CI green);
awaiting `LLM-Review`. Not closing until it is Verified +1 AND merged.

## Corrections to this ticket's description

Implementation disproved three claims in the original description. Recorded here
rather than by editing it, so the trail keeps what was believed at filing time
versus what turned out to be true.

1. **"shellcheck is neither installed nor in the lint gate" — half wrong.**
   `shellcheck-py==0.11.0.1` is ALREADY pinned exactly in pyproject's `[dev]` extra,
   installed by `make install`, and `_build-and-test.yml` already runs a **gating**
   "ShellCheck 0.11.0 smoke check" step. Only the lint-gate wiring was missing. That
   made AC 4 (graceful degradation) and AC 6 (document the dependency) far lighter
   than scoped, and made fail-closed unambiguously safe — CI already guarantees the
   binary is present.

2. **Workflow `run:` blocks were never ungated.** `make lint` runs actionlint, which
   embeds ShellCheck for every `.github/workflows/**` step. The real gap was
   standalone `*.sh` only — 35 files. The description implied no ShellCheck coverage
   existed anywhere, overstating the hole.

3. **The repo already runs mutation testing in CI** (`scripts/mutation_gate.py`,
   `.github/workflows/_mutation.yml`) — a disposable environment, which is the
   posture cargo-mutants explicitly recommends for destructive mutants.

## What was built

- `scripts/check_shellcheck.py` (118 LOC) — discovers `*.sh`, excludes vendored and
  scratch trees, runs ShellCheck at `-S warning`, fails closed when the binary is
  absent (matching `test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py`: "shellcheck-py is a
  required test dependency, not an optional skip").
- `tests/unit/test_check_shellcheck.py` (138 LOC, 12 tests) — pins AC 2 both ways:
  `rm -rf "${dir}"/*` fails with SC2115, and the `: "${dir:?}"` +
  `cd -- "$dir" && rm -rf -- ./*` form passes. Also asserts `SEVERITY == "warning"`,
  because SC2115 is emitted at warning and a gate at `-S error` would run green over
  the exact line that wiped /opt/homebrew.

## The nine pre-existing findings

- `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` — six SC1083 on `^{commit}` git peeling
  syntax. Fixed by quoting (`"HEAD^{commit}"`), not suppressed; quoting is correct
  shell independent of the linter.
- `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` — three justified line-scoped disables (SC2154,
  SC2034, SC2066). It is a `templatefile()` source, so ShellCheck lints it pre-render
  and resolves neither the Terraform interpolation nor the `$${...}` escaping. Genuine
  false positives; the file stays gated for real future findings rather than excluded.

## Verification

`make lint` 0, `make typecheck` 0, complexity ratchet 0, 12/12 new tests pass.

## Payoff

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` is not on `main` — it exists only on the unmerged
`fix-mcp-clone-blocks-boot` branch. When that lands, its
`rm -rf "${dir}"/.[!.]* "${dir}"/*` line cannot merge without tripping SC2115.

Note: posted via the local CLI — the MCP server did not expose `comment_ticket` to
this session. Same logical store (both sync `origin/tickets`).

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The repository has **45 shell scripts** and no ShellCheck gate. A destructive
`rm -rf "${dir}"/*` pattern — the shape that caused a real `rm -rf /*` incident on
a developer workstation on 2026-08-26 — is detected by ShellCheck **SC2115** but
nothing in `make lint` runs it. Add ShellCheck to the lint gate and clear the
existing findings.

## Why SC2115 specifically, and why warning severity

Verified against the incident's exact line:

```sh
dir="$REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"
rm -rf "${dir}"/.[!.]* "${dir}"/*
```
```
probe.sh:3:24: warning: Use "${var:?}" to ensure this never expands to /* . [SC2115]
```

The hardened form is clean:
```sh
: "${dir:?empty}"
(cd -- "${dir:?}" && rm -rf -- ./*) || exit 1
```

**SC2115 is emitted at `warning`, not `error`.** A gate configured at
`-S error` would NOT have caught this. The gate must run at `-S warning`.

## Current findings (measured, shellcheck 0.11.0)

Scope: 45 `*.sh` files excluding `.venv/`, `.git/`, `.claude/`.

- `-S error`: **1** finding
- `-S warning`: **9** findings, confined to **2 files**

| File | Findings |
|---|---|
| `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` | SC2154 (line 25), SC2034 (line 88), SC2066 error (line 104) |
| `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` | SC1083 x6 (lines 75, 76, 80 — literal braces) |

None are the destructive-`rm` class; the 6 `rm -rf` sites on `main` all use the
safe quoted `rm -rf "$tmp"` form against `mktemp -d` results.

## Scope

In scope: wiring ShellCheck into `make lint`, clearing the 9 findings, documenting
the dev-tool dependency.

Out of scope: hardening `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` — that file does not
exist on `main`; it lives only on the unmerged `fix-mcp-clone-blocks-boot` branch.
Once the gate exists, that branch's `rm -rf "${dir}"/.[!.]* "${dir}"/*` line
cannot land without tripping SC2115, which is the point.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `make lint` runs ShellCheck at `-S warning` over every tracked `*.sh` file,
   excluding vendored paths (`.venv/`, `.git/`, `.claude/`), and fails the build on
   any finding.
2. A file containing `rm -rf "${dir}"/*` fails `make lint` with SC2115; the
   `: "${dir:?}"` + `cd -- "$dir" && rm -rf -- ./*` form passes. Covered by a test.
3. The 9 existing findings are resolved — fixed where the code is genuinely wrong,
   or suppressed with a targeted `# shellcheck disable=SCxxxx` carrying a one-line
   justification comment. No blanket file-level or repo-level disables.
4. `make lint` degrades with a clear, actionable message when ShellCheck is not
   installed, naming the install command. It must not silently skip — a skipped
   gate is indistinguishable from a passing one.
5. Enforcement lives in `make lint` (which both the pre-commit hook and CI invoke),
   not in a CI-provider-specific workflow step, satisfying `project.portability`.
6. The ShellCheck dependency is documented in the dev-environment setup alongside
   the existing ruff/mypy tooling.

## Definition of Done

- `make lint` green on a clean tree with ShellCheck wired in.
- The AC-2 regression test passes and fails correctly when the guard is removed.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` names ShellCheck as a required dev tool.
- No new complexity-baseline or module-size violations introduced.

## Notes

Filed from the 2026-08-26 workstation incident, where a mutation test removed a
guard function from a script performing real filesystem deletion and then executed
it unsandboxed. Research finding worth recording: **no mutation-testing tool in any
language isolates runtime side effects** — cargo-mutants, mutmut, Stryker, PIT and
mull all isolate only the source tree, and cargo-mutants documents this hazard
explicitly at https://mutants.rs/cautions.html. ShellCheck is the cheapest control
that would have prevented the specific line from ever landing; sandboxing the
mutation run is the broader fix and is tracked separately.
